detail:
The NIDDK Central Repository describes the Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) as a multicenter trial testing whether an intensive lifestyle program or metformin could prevent or delay type 2 diabetes in high-risk adults with prediabetes. The study found both approaches reduced the development of diabetes compared with placebo, with the lifestyle intervention proving more effective in the original trial.

Its long-term follow-up, the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study (DPPOS), continues to examine whether prevention or delay persists over time and how it relates to complications such as retinopathy, kidney and nerve disease, cardiovascular disease, and cancer. NIDDK summaries of the broader field also point to ongoing study of newer glucose-lowering medicine classes and their heart and kidney outcomes, alongside genetics and prevention research in high-risk populations.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about type 2 diabetes prevention and research studies.

title: Where type 2 diabetes research is heading
